## Verdict

Inkwell costs least for a team of 22, at $242 per month. Its 20-seat minimum sits just below the team size, so all 22 seats bill at the list rate with nothing wasted. Borealis is the next option at $600, and Dorado — despite the lowest minimum — is dearest at $528 to $600 depending on nothing but its per-seat rate.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $24 | 5 |
| Inkwell | $11 | 20 |
| Borealis | $15 | 40 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for is the team size (22) or the vendor minimum, whichever is larger.

- **Dorado:** minimum 5 is below 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $24 = **$528 per month**.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 20 is below 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $11 = **$242 per month**.
- **Borealis:** minimum 40 exceeds 22, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Eighteen seats, worth $270, go unused.

Inkwell is $286 per month cheaper than Dorado and $358 cheaper than Borealis — $3,432 and $4,296 over twelve months. Effective rate per person: Inkwell $11.00, Dorado $24.00, Borealis $27.27.

## Risks

Inkwell's margin is thin against its own floor. At 22 people the team sits two seats above the 20-seat minimum; any drop below 20 still bills $220, raising the effective rate.

Borealis is the only vendor whose ranking turns on its minimum rather than its rate. Past 40 seats it costs $15 against Dorado's $24, so it overtakes Dorado on price at scale — but never Inkwell, which stays cheapest per seat at every size here.

This is a price comparison and nothing more. The list carries no feature, support, capacity or security detail, so a cheaper seat may buy less product. All figures assume monthly billing as stated; annual commitments, negotiated discounts, onboarding fees and overage charges are absent from the source and could reorder the result.
